articles.title: How Bulgaria become a global leader in battery storage and what this means for the country's grid and energy market?
articles.summary: In under two years, Bulgaria has become one of the world's most battery-intensive energy markets. Can the surge last — and what will it mean for conventional power generators?

image.caption: Powerhouse in southeastern Europe: Bulgaria has one of the world's highest ratios of battery storage to total power capacity in the world. Pictured here: a solar park with storage batteries in Maglizh, BulgariaImage: Tsvetelina Belutova/Capital

blocks.text: The international energy sector currently has a curious case study in an unlikely place: Bulgaria, a country in southeastern Europe with a population of just 6.4 million, now has one of the world's highest ratios of battery storage to total power capacity, outpacing markets like California, Germany and China.

In less than two years, Bulgaria's battery storage capacity has gone from zero to making up nearly a quarter of the country's total installed power capacity, fueled by EU funding and private capital worth close to €3 billion ($3.4 billion), according to calculations by Bulgaria's leading business publication Capital.
Bulgaria was lucky enough to escape the worst of the heatwaves and droughts that forced a cut in nuclear and hydro output in Hungary and Romania this summer.
During that period, it turned its batteries into a key grid stabilizer for neighboring markets and profited by storing cheap solar power and selling it in the evening when prices spike.

blocks.caption: Bulgaria used its batteries this summer as a key grid stabilizer for neighboring marketsImage: imageBROKER/Nikola Spasov/imagebroker/IMAGO

blocks.text: And while experts say the Bulgarian battery boom went "under the radar," it remains to be seen how this rapid development will affect the other generators of power, whether the current business model is sustainable and whether private investment will dictate a shift in the national strategy for the country's energy transition.
What is the Bulgarian battery boom?
In January 2026, a report by the energy think tank Ember estimated Bulgaria's battery capacity — both operational and in the pipeline — to be 1.66 GW.
Eight months later, capacity had more than tripled to 5.4 GW, according to data from ENTSO-E. Bulgaria's Ministry of Energy told AFP it had already reached 5.7 GW.
"Two years ago, no one imagined we would have even half of this capacity," Ivaylo Stanchev, editor-in-chief of the business publication Capital, told DW.

Stanchev compiled one of the country's most comprehensive lists of battery projects, filling a gap left by the absence of an official public database. The list itself reflects investment levels that have outpaced official forecasts.

blocks.caption: Ivaylo Stanchev, editor-in-chief of the business publication Capital, says that Bulgaria having this kind of battery capacity was unimaginable just two years ago Image: Capital

blocks.text: While the rapid battery buildout was sparked by the Next Generation EU recovery fund and the subsequent RESTORE programs, which approved €700 million ($797 million) in funding for 113 projects, Stanchev estimates that private investment amounted to almost three times that figure: roughly €2 billion.
Although most of the lithium batteries come from China, the investors are mostly from Bulgaria or from other European countries, which see potential in the growing niche.
How much can the batteries store?

"When fully charged, the batteries can store enough energy to power the whole country for several hours," said Stanchev, drawing a comparison that, although practically impossible, illustrates the scale of the development.
Its effects are already tangible: Bulgaria produces a large amount of solar energy and buys more from Greece and Romania.

Daily prices during the summer tend to be low or even negative during the sunniest hours of the day, allowing batteries to buy cheap energy, store it and discharge it in the evening, when local and international markets need it, at a higher price.
The main export destination is Romania, which was particularly badly hit during the summer as it had to reduce nuclear capacity because of the drought along the Danube.
Bulgaria, historically a net exporter, has thus turned into a regional battery hub, with an operational storage capacity that is now greater than that of Greece and Romania combined.
What is the impact of this rapid development?

There is no measurement that isolates the batteries' specific electricity price contribution, but Bulgaria's average price fell relative to other countries in the region during the first summer of large-scale battery operation.
And while households in Bulgaria are subject to fixed electricity prices set by the state and have not yet seen a reduction in their electricity bills, industrial companies benefited from the change.

"Between August 1 and August 16, the average day-ahead electricity price per MWh in Bulgaria was €132.2 — almost €14 lower than the price in Romania, even though they used to be almost equal," said Stanchev, adding that the difference comes mainly from the evening hours where the batteries' effect is most at play.
Additionally, the batteries bring more security to the grid both domestically and regionally — as well as more revenue from exports and potential tax revenue from the company profits, he explained.

blocks.caption: It is estimated that approx. €700 million in EU funding and roughly €2 billion in private money have powered Bulgaria's battery storage boomImage: Tsvetelina Belutova/Capital

blocks.text: Yet, these effects are part of the summer period snapshot, raising questions about the sustainability of the model throughout the year.
Is this all good news?

"Such record development should always be taken with a pinch of salt," said Kaloyan Staykov, chair of the Management Board of the Energy Management Institute in Bulgaria, adding that the year-long effects of the vast battery buildout "are yet to be seen."
Staykov argues that, while a positive development for the market overall, the shift has come at a cost for conventional energy generators.

"While the electricity price during the evening peak is now down, the generation that used to be more profitable during those hours needs to make up for the lower revenue stream, which pushes up the baseload price," he said.

This issue points to a broader one. "Investments in batteries go beyond any national strategy for what the sector will look like in 10 or 20 years' time," he said, adding that "the role of national strategic roadmaps is changing from a leading one, to a following one."
This comes at a time when Bulgaria is slowly pursuing a transition away from coal, including the expected phase-out of coal mining.

At the same time, the country is advancing the rehabilitation of a massive pumped-storage hydropower plant (Chaira) and intends to build two new nuclear reactors at the Kozloduy Nuclear Power Plant in the years to come.
The rise in renewable energy and the risk of cannibalization
Between 2022 and 2026, photovoltaic buildout in Bulgaria more than quadrupled, according to data from ENTSO-E.

blocks.caption: Kaloyan Staykov of the Energy Management Institute in Bulgaria cautions that the year-long effects of the vast battery buildout 'are yet to be seen'Image: Maria Sabotinova

blocks.text: Private investors seized on the potential offered by this technology by building battery storage at solar parks and elsewhere — a development that was facilitated by the fact that it is in general easy to obtain permits for such batteries in Bulgaria.

Delyan Dobrev, a former MP and energy minister from the center-right GERB party who has recently stepped down from politics, announced in an interview with Focus news agency in September what he describes as advanced talks with US giant Tesla for an additional battery complex — one he says is expected to be among "the largest in Europe."

Yet Staykov warned that it remains to be seen how much more growth the market and grid can absorb in the short-term, as the system adjusts to this new reality and investors realize the first-mover advantage may already be shrinking.

As more batteries connect to the grid, revenue per unit can fall. Yet both Staykov and Stanchev agree that introducing ancillary services that allow batteries to discharge energy to stabilize the grid will be key in the future.
Such a development would be new for Bulgaria and might ease concerns about potential cannibalization, in other words batteries competing away their own margins as capacity grows.
"This year we managed to capitalize on the situation, although no one can predict what the markets will look like this autumn or in three years' time," said Staykov.
How batteries stabilize the power grid in northern Germany

articles.title: Iranian President Pezeshkian brought a diplomatic tone to New York for UNGA. What did his remarks signal?
articles.summary: Iran's president used his trip to New York this week for the UN General Assembly to signal openness to talks over the nuclear dispute. However, the chances of a major breakthrough on the war remain…

image.caption: Iranian President Masud Peseschkian addressed the UN General Assembly in New York while his country is at war with the USImage: Kyle Mazza/CNP/IMAGO

blocks.text: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who travelled to New York to attend the UN General Assembly, met with American journalists and media representatives.
In an interview with the conservative US broadcaster Fox News, he signaled a willingness to make concessions in the nuclear dispute with the United States.

Washington has made clear that Iran must never be allowed to possess nuclear weapons. Asked whether Iran was prepared to hand over its highly enriched uranium, Pezeshkian said his country would comply with its obligationsunder international law and the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.
In its most recent assessment, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), estimated that Iran had more than 440 kilograms of uranium enriched to up to 60%.

Since the US-Israeli attacks on Iranian nuclear facilities in 2025, Iran suspended its cooperation with the IAEA. The agency has continued to demand access to Iranian facilities and updated information on its nuclear stockpile and the whereabouts of its nuclear material.
Asked point-blank "Do you want a nuclear bomb or not?" during the exclusive interview on Fox News' "Special Report," Pezeshkian firmly rejected the premise.

"Not at all. Not at all. Our martyred, esteemed supreme leader had announced several times that, from a religious decree, it is unholy. It is illegal," he told Bret Baier, referencing religious edicts issued against weapons of mass destruction.
Despite Pezeshkians claims, the IAEA has assessed that Iran's fissile material is being enriched far beyond what is needed for civilian use.
Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran if no deal is reached
Diplomacy: A first step?

A major breakthrough in the conflict between Iran and the United States is not expected anytime soon, Iran expert Arman Mahmoudian, a lecturer in Middle East Studies at the University of South Florida, told DW.

"Pezeshkian does not have the authority to initiate comprehensive de-escalation with the United States. In particular, hardliners and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) appear to continue to wield considerable influence over Iran's decision-making process," he added.
Nevertheless, Mahmoudian thinks Pezeshkian's visit could help establish a more direct channel of communication between Tehran and Washington.

He also sees the possibility of creating a framework for future negotiations in New York, adding that the two sides could develop a roadmap that would pave the way for more substantive talks and, in the longer term, potentially contribute to de-escalation.

There are already signs of this, including meetings between Iranian and US delegations earlier this week. The White House, meanwhile, confirmed that "positive and constructive" talks were continuing through intermediaries.
Hormuz — and Houthis — as leverage

The future of the Strait of Hormuz is also at the center of the discussions. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reportedly said that Tehran had presented Washington with a proposal to resume negotiations.
Under the proposal, the strategically important waterway could be reopened within seven days if certain conditions were met. It remains unclear what those conditions are.

In the past, Iran has demanded the release of frozen Iranian assets, an end to the US blockade of Iranian ports and vessels, and a commitment by Washington not to interfere in Iran's internal affairs.
Strike on Iran school: Did US commit a war crime?
The Strait of Hormuz, through which around 20 million barrels of oil normally pass every day — roughly 20% of global oil consumption — has become one of Iran's most important sources of leverage.
The United States has failed to eliminate all of Iran's capabilities to threaten shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, Kelly Grieco, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center, told DW in July.
This is despite the US attacks having caused significant damage to Iran's navy and defense industry.
"At a certain point, it becomes really hard to find some of these targets," said Grieco. "They're mobile. They're distributed."

Without a long-term strategy, Grieco warned, the United States could therefore become trapped in a recurring cycle: Iran rebuilds its military capabilities, Washington launches another round of attacks, and the cycle repeats itself.
Nearly seven months after the start of the Iran war, the conflict has also spread to a second strategically important shipping route.

The Iran-backed Houthi movement has expanded its control over Yemen's Red Sea coast and the strategically important area around the Bab al-Mandab Strait. This gives Iran another important lever along major international shipping routes.
Balancing pressure and negotiations

Mahmoudian expects Iran to continue pursuing a dual strategy of military pressure and diplomacy, saying that Tehran is likely to continue using the Strait of Hormuz as leverage and to prevent a full return to normal shipping traffic.
Red Sea strains rattle energy markets

"At the same time, Iran will most likely continue rebuilding its military and strategic infrastructure inside the country," he said. "Reports suggest that Iranian authorities are already moving quickly to reconstruct some damaged facilities."
On the diplomatic front, he added that Iran is likely to continue negotiations with the US, either directly or through intermediaries.

Tehran is aware that the current situation, with the continuing threat of military attacks, sanctions and economic pressure, is not sustainable in the long term, Mahmoudian said, adding that Iran will therefore continue to have an interest in reaching a political agreement with Washington.

A deal with Iran will require time and difficult negotiations, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in New York on September 23, playing down expectations of a quick agreement. At the same time, he stressed that President Donald Trump has military options at his disposal alongside the diplomatic route.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: After Xi-Trump summit, US-China rivalry remains frozen. Is this to Beijing's advantage?
articles.summary: The US president showcased White House construction projects and hosted a lavish dinner with tech CEOs, but the summit made little progress on key issues such as trade tensions and AI regulation.

image.caption: Chinese leader Xi Jinping was treated to a personal tour of the US presidential helicopterImage: Evan Vucci/REUTERS

blocks.text: When US President Donald Trump rolled out the red carpet for Chinese leader Xi Jinping at Andrews Air Force Base on Wednesday evening, it was a rare diplomatic gesture that has only happened a handful of times in US history.

Generally, world leaders are received by the president at the White House. Xi's VIP reception underlines the importance Trump places on his personal rapport with China's most powerful leader in a generation.

blocks.caption: The last US president to greet a world leader at Andrews Air Force Base was John F. Kennedy in 1962Image: Alex Brandon/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: After 90 minutes of bilateral talks in the Oval Office, Trump spent Thursday afternoon showing his "good friend" Xi his various White House construction projects, including the helipad completed just days earlier over the South Lawn. He then welcomed Xi aboard the presidential helicopter Marine One for a brief tour.
Trump's 'personal diplomacy'
Trump then told reporters "we had a great meeting," adding that Xi "loves good granite."

The optics continued at a glitzy state dinner Thursday night, where Trump said he and President Xi have "never gotten along better" and lauded building a "relationship that promotes prosperity and security for future generations."

Judging from Xi's mannerisms, it isn't clear the Chinese leader shares Trump's enthusiasm for personal diplomacy. When Trump arrived in Beijing for a summit in May, Xi sent diplomatic envoy, Vice President Han Zheng, to meet the US president.

"Trump's 'personalized diplomacy' is a one-sided construct — one that exists mainly in his own mind. He may believe his personal rapport with Xi is the key factor shaping Sino-American relations, but there's little to no evidence backing that claim," said Aurelio Insisa, senior analyst at the Berlin-based Mercator Institute for China Studies (MERICS).
Xi's whirlwind visit to the US, his first in 10 years, has been heavy on pomp, but relatively low on substance.

As of Friday morning, most summit coverage has focused on what was for dinner and the tech CEO guest list, in lieu of any deliverables on thorny issues like trade deals or cooperation on artificial intelligence. There is still time for announcements when Xi departs Washington later Friday after visiting the National Archives with Trump.
"The Chinese approach has shown no meaningful deviation in the US President's favor, beneath the usual pomp and circumstance of apex-level summitry," Insisa told DW.

blocks.caption: Showing off his new helipad, Trump said Xi is an 'expert on stone' Image: Evan Vucci/REUTERS

blocks.text: Trade truce extended, rare earths a quesiton mark
The most-pressing issue remains managing a trade war launched by Trump's scattershot tariffs in April 2025 that at one point were so high they essentially amounted to an embargo on Chinese goods.

On Wednesday, US Treasury Secretary Bessent said a trade truce due to expire in November would be extended until January "to give us more time to see what we can do on the economic front." Such an extension had been widely expected before the summit.

The trade truce builds on the "Busan deal" Trump and Xi agreed on at a meeting in South Korea last October, where Trump backed off on more tariffs in exchange for Xi easing export control for rare earths, which are critical ingredients for building high-tech kit.
Levering China's chokehold on rare earths to confront Trump's tariff blitz represented a major victory for Xi.

The Financial Times reported earlier this week that the US "believes China has not fully lived up to its commitment of uninterrupted supply," adding that China's shipments of rare earths to the US have dropped recently, amid concerns China could again "choke supplies."
What to expect from the Trump-Xi summit?

On tariffs and trade, Trump made nebulous comments on Thursday about "progress," but no specific deals on sectors or goods have yet been reported as of Friday morning. Reports ahead of the summit of an expected $30 billion in two-way tariff cuts have also yet to be proven.

Melanie Hart, director of Global China Hub at the Atlantic Council, wrote in a briefing earlier this week that the tariff cut announcement has been "so widely expected that if it is derailed, it will indicate something has gone horribly wrong."

Agreements and negotiations are happening through the US-China "Board of Trade," which was announced in May. US trade representative Jamieson Greer has said the board is operating, with initial lists of possible products including US agricultural goods and Chinese LNG and low-tech goods.
China also wants more access to cutting-edge chips made by US companies needed to develop frontier AI models.

Also unresolved is the question of US secondary sanctions targeting Iran's financiers,which would include Chinese banks. Trump has also dismissed reports China provided targeting intelligence to Iran.
"The foundations of this trade truce are brittle, and it will likely not survive the end of the second Trump presidency," Insisa said.

"Beijing will not radically alter its industrial and trade policy to meet Washington's demands, and future US administrations — even Republican ones — will likely deviate from Trump's approach to China."
Talk but no walk on AI
Following safety warnings from AI labs, AI regulation and the US-China tech race were thrust into the spotlight ahead of the summit, but expectations for true cooperation are low.

On Sunday, a US-China AI "dialogue" was announced after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and trade representative Greer met with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng. Other items included a possible crisis communications line. It is unclear when the group will meet again, with the APEC summit in November providing a possible venue.
How US, China could end the AI race
Trump sees developing AI as a winner-take-all race to the top, and has also reduced the incentive for China to slow down its own development, having called the AI lab's safety warnings a "hoax."

Further complicating any parallel AI regulatory frameworks between the US and China is a lack of trust or transparency, where it is impossible to verify if one side is complying with agreed-upon rules. There are also diverging ideas on what regulation means, according to MERICS analyst Antonia Hmaidi.
Xi's ask on Taiwan
Almost every Trump-Xi summit has been overshadowed by fears that the transactional US president will trade in supporting the self-ruled democracy Taiwan for a deal with Beijing.

This has been compounded by Trump having delayed a $14 billion (€12.2 billion) US arms package for Taiwan passed by Congress in January. Following the May summit, Trump called the package a "good bargaining chip."
Beijing claims Taiwan as Chinese territory and has vowed to crush any attempts at "independence."

But despite these fears, the US under Trump has yet to shift its narrative on Taiwan, maintaining a posture of "strategic ambiguity" by providing defense support but not officially taking a position on Taiwanese sovereignty.
This creates a delicate diplomatic balance based on language.

Chinese state media reported Xi told Trump he hopes the US will "adhere to the correct position of opposing 'Taiwan independence." If Trump accepted "opposition," it would represent a major break from the current, more passive, formulation of "not supporting" independence.
Trump's off-the-cuff communication style has led to concerns an errant utterance could be interpreted as a change in position, but this has yet to happen.
Freezing the US-China rivalry

By holding summit after summit building on positive superficial optics, Beijing is maintaining what Chinese policymakers have recently begun calling "constructive strategic stability" in its multifront competition with the US.
"The summit is evidence that the current trajectory in the bilateral relationship continues to favor China," said MERICS analyst Insisa.

blocks.caption: Tech CEOs joined the leaders of the US and China for a state dinner at the White House Image: Alex Brandon/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: At the White House dinner, Xi's statement echoed similar remarks made during May's state dinner in Beijing.

"President Trump has pledged to make America great again ... China is committed to achieving great national rejuvenation ... These two goals are both ambitious and can surely be mutually reinforcing," Xi said.

But Xi's Trump-aligned rhetoric belies what Beijing sees as a fading US-led world order, or what it calls "great changes unseen in a century." While Trump is focused on US midterm elections in November, Xi has his eye on securing another five years at the helm during next year's CCP national congress.

"China has perfected its 'Trump playbook' since his return to power and the tariff spat triggered by his 'Liberation Day' announcement in April 2025," Insisa said. "For the time being, Beijing has found a way to keep the Trump administration engaged while avoiding concrete steps on the most pressing issues: AI governance, trade relations, export controls," he added.
The next time the two leaders are expected to meet will be on the sidelines of November's APEC summit in Shenzhen. These issues will most likely all still be on the table, and Xi can wait.
Trump hosts China's Xi for state visit

articles.title: Meloni accused of election shift to right after ’shameful’ cap on foreign children in classrooms
articles.summary:
Critics say decree also banning burqa in schools shows Italian PM running scared ahead of next year’s vote

Rights campaigners have accused the Italian government of ramping up divisive…
articles.byline: Ashifa Kassam European community affairs correspondent

blocks.text: Rights campaigners have accused the Italian government of ramping up divisive rhetoric in an attempt to court far-right voters ahead of next year’s general election after it passed a decree aimed at capping the number of newly arrived migrants in classrooms and banning the burqa and niqab in schools.

The prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, who leads the far-right Brothers of Italy party, said her government had approved what she called “commonsense measures that do not divide but genuinely help to integrate”.
Writing on social media, she added: “A limit of 30% in classrooms for students who do not adequately know Italian, plus tools to learn our language and a halt to burqas and niqabs in school.”

The announcement was a toned-down version of comments she had made earlier in the week at an event organised by Brothers of Italy’s youth division. “It cannot be that in the classroom it is Italian children who feel left out because they’ve become the minority,” Meloni said as she vowed to “legally set the number of foreign students per class”.

Thursday’s decree also sets out that in cases where students show persistent problems with integrating or struggle to learn the language, their parents will be referred to social services and will have to take free literacy and Italian language classes. Failure to comply on the part of parents could result in fines of up to €1,000.
The education minister, Giuseppe Valditara, said the measures, set to take effect in the 2027-28 school year, would affect about 1,000 classrooms, or about 0.3% of the total nationwide.
Rights campaigners were swift to link the measures to next year’s election, in which Meloni’s premiership is facing an unexpected challenger on the right.

“She’s creating an emergency that is not a real emergency at all,” said Daniela Ionita, of the campaign group Italians without Citizenship, pointing out that an estimated 60% of the pupils who could be described as foreign were born in Italy but faced a myriad of hurdles when it came to accessing citizenship. “Because there are now new parties pushing from the right, I think Meloni is scared,” she said.

blocks.caption: Jannatur Nayeem, 33, an Italian citizen of Bangladeshi origin, chats with other mothers as they wait for a sports session to end at a school in Rome on Thursday. Photograph: Alessandra Tarantino/AP

blocks.text: The government said students born and raised in Italy or who had attended at least two years of nursery school or completed three years of schooling in Italy would be exempt from the measures.

Ionita said the ramped-up rhetoric was an attempt by the government to mask how little it had accomplished during its time in power. “If you remove every decree linked to security or to migrants, the government’s political and economic programme will fall apart, and very little concrete remains of one of the longest-serving governments of the last years in Italy,” she said.

Marco Tarchi, a political scientist who focuses on the extreme right and teaches at the University of Florence, said the school measures were “undoubtedly” driven by fears of a new political challenge on the right.
Since February, a new party, Futuro Nazionale (FN), has galvanised the extreme right, with polls suggesting it could capture about 8% of the vote in an election expected as early as spring 2027.

Led by Roberto Vannacci, a former army general best known for self-publishing a book rife with racism, homophobia, Islamophobia and antisemitism, the party’s popularity in polls has eclipsed that of Brothers of Italy’s two coalition partners, the League and the conservative Forza Italia.

blocks.caption: Roberto Vannacci’s party Futuro Nazionale has galvanised the extreme right. Photograph: Remo Casilli/Reuters

blocks.text: Those who have shifted allegiances include some who had enthusiastically lined up behind Meloni years ago as she spoke of “ethnic substitution” and vowed to install an all-out naval blockade to prevent migrant arrivals from north Africa.

Tarchi said: “Many of the FN’s potential voters are former supporters of Giorgia Meloni’s party who are disappointed that, once in power, the leader softened many of her previous stances regarding the European Union, which she had harshly criticised; immigration, on which she had made radical proposals that were later abandoned; and other issues.”

He said Vannacci had capitalised on this, capturing voters with an extreme manifesto that promised “remigration” and limits on the number of foreigners in the country, as well as curtailing LGBTQ+ rights and negating the right to abortion. He said that in order to win back this support, Meloni could have to adopt positions closer to those she held while in opposition.

A glimpse of what this could look like came this summer when Meloni seized on the sudden entry of tens of thousands of people into the tiny Spanish territory of Ceuta in north Africa, said Elisa De Pieri, a researcher at Amnesty International.

“Meloni immediately exploited the situation in Ceuta, which had absolutely nothing to do with Italy and nothing to do with the Schengen space, but she made it into a supposed crisis for Italy,” she said. “And so that’s the mode that I think we’re going to see in the next months.”

De Pieri predicted that Meloni “won’t be talking too much” about Italy’s offshore detention agreement with Albania on the grounds that it had not been successful as she would have hoped. “It’s been very costly, and it’s been struck down repeatedly by national and international courts,” she said.

blocks.caption: A reception camp for migrants transferred from Italy in Gjader, Albania, in 2024. Photograph: Florion Goga/Reuters

blocks.text: Instead, she expects that Meloni will adopt a more aggressive tone on migration more generally, leading to a polarising electoral campaign whose impact would be disproportionately borne among migrant communities.

The view was echoed by critics of the new measures who pointed out the rarity of burqas or niqabs in Italian classrooms and said the government was simply repackaging previous, unenforced policies, given that the 30% threshold was previously floated by the education ministry in 2010. Save the Children said the overall impact would be to “create ‘first-class’ and ‘second-class’ students”.

The leader of the Democratic party, Elly Schlein, described the decree as “shameful” and accused the government of “living on a different planet”. She said Italian parents were grappling with a very different set of issues, citing crumbling school buildings, the high costs of textbooks and low salaries of teachers.

“Faced with all this, the government’s response is to kick foreign children out of the classroom,” Schlein said. “Who do they think they’re kidding? After four years of cuts and no serious investment in school buildings, they’re inventing a witch-hunt that targets the youngest children.”

articles.title: Will Sara Duterte, Mayor Baste appear at the impeachment trial? It depends, says the VP
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte was mum on whether or not she and her brother Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte will attend her impeachment trial.

blocks.text: Published September 25, 2026 7:28pm
Vice President Sara Duterte was mum on whether or not she and her brother Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte will attend her impeachment trial.

The impeachment court has already issued a subpoena to Baste Duterte, while the House prosecution panel has expressed its intent to have Sara Duterte summoned to answer the charges lodged against her.
“Anong ibig sabihin? Manood ako doon sa kanilang sarsuela? Well, depende, wala pa namang pagpapatawag sa akin,” Sara Duterte said in an ambush interview in Davao City.
(What do you mean? That I will go there and watch their dance? Well, it depends, no one has called me yet.)
The vice president also said that she was already represented by her lawyers in the trial.
“Ang impeachment ay isang legal na process at yung pagpunta ng aking mga abogado doon, yun ang aking appearance at participation doon sa proseso na yun,” she said.
(The impeachment is a legal process and my lawyers are already there and that is already my appearance and participation in that process.)
Sara Duterte was also uncertain whether her brother Baste Duterte would attend.
“Wala akong info kung a-attend siya, pero ang napag-usapan namin noon at that time, mayroong subpoena sa kanya so sinabihan ko siya bago pa man lumabas,” she said.
(I do not have info if he will attend, but when we talked about it at the time, there was a subpoena against him and I told him before it came out.)
Baste Duterte will consult the city legal office, according to the vice president.
Asked about the overturning of the decision that set the conviction threshold at 16, Sara Duterte declined to comment, saying that her lawyers might scold her.
Bags of cash?

During the ambush interview, Duterte was also asked about an allegation that she received a large amount of cash that was delivered to her family. The question, coming from a person who did not disclose her media outlet, traced the allegation to Palace Press Officer Claire Castro.
Sara Duterte said that she has not seen any such report, but proceeded to lambast Castro anyway.

“Hindi ko napanood, yung sinabi niya so hindi ako maka-comment but coming from Claire Castro, alam naman natin na isa siya kahihiyan sa ating bansa so sabi ko nga lagi sa media, wag niyo bigyan ng espasyo yung mga ganyan,” she said.
(I did not watch what she said so I could not comment but coming from Claire Castro, we know that she is a shame to our country so I always tell the media, do not give those things space.)
GMA News Online has already sought clarification from Castro regarding the matter and will update the story once she responds. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Tour Montparnasse renovation halted amid disagreements between owners
articles.summary:
Plans to modernise ‘Paris’s ugliest building’ at a standstill after clashes over plans and pricing

It has been called a carbuncle on the Paris skyline, a sombre skyscraper where visitors to…

blocks.text: It has been called a carbuncle on the Paris skyline, a sombre skyscraper where visitors to its viewing platform often joke that the city looks better when you can’t see the building itself.

The much-maligned Tour Montparnasse, a lone, dark monolith with tinted windows rising above a historic neighbourhood in the south of the city, is once again at the centre of controversy after its long-awaited renovation was halted this week because of disagreements between its many private co-owners.
The tower, which opened in 1973, is the tallest skyscraper in inner-city Paris and is also considered its ugliest building.

blocks.caption: Paris’s tallest inner-city skyscraper is due to undergo a massive structural transition. Photograph: Frédéric Vielcanet/Alamy

blocks.text: For more than a decade, plans have been thrashed out to overhaul the building and brighten its looming presence and modernise the area around it. Architects had planned to entirely refit the 210-metre structure with a new glass exterior, adding vegetation throughout, with a garden terrace on the 16th floor and an agricultural greenhouse at the top. The plans included a hotel on three floors of the 59-storey building, as well as new office and leisure spaces.
But alongside a significant operation to remove asbestos, the estimated price of the project more than doubled to €800m (£688m).

The building’s private co-owners, which include French investment funds and insurers, met this week for a final vote on the start of a first phase of renovation, with asbestos removal, interior stripping and a partial facade removal. After clashes over plans and pricing, more than three-quarters of the co-owners voted against the project.

It was the last opportunity to launch the project before the building permit granted for the tower’s renovation expires at the end of November. There are now concerns that the building, which has been emptied and closed for renovation, will loom deserted. This summer, fire officers intervened after bits of glass fell off the building and landed on the street below, although no one was hurt.

blocks.caption: Opposition councillors on the left have suggested the ‘obsolete’ tower should come down. Photograph: Bim/Getty Images

blocks.text: “Everyone needs to come to their senses,” said Philippe Goujon, the rightwing mayor of Paris’s 15th district where the tower is located. He told Agence France-Presse: “I cannot accept seeing a project that took 10 years to develop thrown away, or allowing this world-renowned landmark to fall into neglect.”

Four of the co-owners who still want a renovation, including the tycoon Xavier Niel, said in a joint statement: “We would like all the co-owners, financial partners and public authorities to meet soon to examine all the solutions to transform the Montparnasse Tower.”
Some co-owners hope that a new, scaled-down project could be agreed upon.

blocks.caption: Many commercial spaces within the tower have been left derelict. Photograph: Abaca Press/Alamy

blocks.text: Separately, the architect Renzo Piano has been tasked with overhauling the shopping centre beneath the tower and other buildings nearby, opening up new pedestrian spaces and moving from grey concrete to a greener, planted space. Local officials want to avoid delays to that project if the tower’s renovation stalls.
The office of the Socialist mayor of Paris, Emmanuel Grégoire, said it wanted “an alternative solution to be proposed” so the site does not stay at a standstill.
Opposition councillors on the left have suggested the “obsolete” tower should instead come down and be replaced by a park that would have a cooling effect during summer heatwaves.

articles.summary:
Thomas appeared at Basingstoke magistrates court on Friday after being charged with criminal damage

The far-right activist Daniel Thomas has pleaded not guilty to criminal damage after he…

blocks.text: The far-right activist Daniel Thomas has pleaded not guilty to criminal damage after he allegedly slashed a boat in the Channel with an emergency responder on board.

Thomas, 37, of no fixed address, appeared at Basingstoke magistrates court on Friday after being charged on Thursday night. He also denied failing to disclose the pin to his phone to police, under section 53 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000.
Thomas was supported by fellow far-right activist Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, also known as Tommy Robinson, who arrived at the court on Friday morning and sat in the public gallery.
On Thursday evening several hundred people, many wearing black, gathered outside a police investigation centre in Basingstoke believing that Thomas was inside.
Dozens of police officers could be seen monitoring the group outside the centre as the protest continued for several hours.

articles.title: 'Ayoko na rin pong andito ako': Vince Dizon asked about lapsed appointment as DPWH chief
articles.summary: Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon was questioned on Friday about his lapsed appointment as department chief, which was supposed to end on September 1, 2026,…

blocks.text: Published September 25, 2026 7:08pm

Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon was questioned on Friday about his lapsed appointment as department chief, which was supposed to end on September 1, 2026, according to Senator Imee Marcos.
In response, the DPWH chief said he would be more than happy to leave the post if it is declared that his tenure has already ended, adding that the job was extremely challenging.
"Permission to speak frankly. Ma'am, this is music to my ears kasi medyo ayoko na rin pong nandito ako eh, so gusto ko na pong wala ako dito. Okay na po ito, masaya pa po ako," Dizon said.

(Permission to speak frankly. Ma'am, this is music to my ears because I also somewhat don't want to be here anymore, so I would really prefer not to be here. This is fine with me, and I would even be happy about it.)

"To be quite frank, it would be very welcome kung totoo po 'yung sinasabi ninyo na hindi na ako secretary ng DPWH. I will be more than happy to accept that kasi napakahirap po ng trabaho na to," he added.

(To be quite frank, it would be very welcome if what you're saying is true—that I am no longer the secretary of the DPWH. I will be more than happy to accept that because this job is extremely difficult.)
Marcos raised the issue after she followed up with Dizon a letter of inquiry she sent to his office on September 2.
The senator said she did not receive any reply from the secretary within seven days, pursuant to their administrative code.
"I'm sorry, but the Administrative Code is very clear that it is only one year, and if you are appointed in an acting capacity, September 1, 2025, it has lapsed in 2026," Marcos asked Dizon.
"Today is [September] 25, 2026—overdue na po kayo ng ilang araw. What is the present status, therefore, of your appointment?" she added.
(Today is [September] 25, 2026—you are overdue by several days. What is the present status, therefore, of your appointment?)
Dizon said that he has yet to confer with the Office of the President to clarify the status of his appointment.
Citing information from DPWH Chief-of-Staff Undersecretary Ricardo Bernabe III, Dizon pointed out that his appointment continues until the session of Congress ends and goes into recess.
"Usec. Bernabe just told me that… my appointment po as the Secretary is continuing until the session of Congress ends and in recess. After which I need to be reappointed," Dizon said.
Dizon took his oath as DPWH chief on September 1, 2025, replacing former secretary Manuel Bonoan, who resigned from the post amid public pressure over the flood control scandal.

Dizon was serving as the Department of Transportation secretary at the time, but his stint was cut short to conduct a "full organizational sweep" within the DPWH as ordered by President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr.
According to Dizon, in the past year, at least 61 DPWH employees found to have ties to anomalies were removed from office, with some facing pending charges.
Meanwhile, at least 19 contractors have been referred to the Office of the Ombudsman, and 11 contractors have been blacklisted, the DPWH chief added. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Batas na nag-uurong sa Brgy. at SK elections upang gawin sa Nov. 2028, pirmado na ni Marcos
articles.summary: Pinirmahan na ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ang bagong batas para ipagpaliban ang nakatakdang Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) sa darating na Nobyembre, upang iusog sa Nobyembre…

blocks.text: Pinirmahan na ni Pangulong Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ang bagong batas para ipagpaliban ang nakatakdang Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE) sa darating na Nobyembre, upang iusog sa Nobyembre 2028. Ang termino ng mga opisyal ng barangay, pinapahaba rin ng limang taon.

"Sa paglagda natin sa Republic Act No, 12326, na nagtatakda ng limang taong termino para sa mga opisyal ng barangay at Sangguniang Kabataan, malinaw ang ating inaasahan sa ating mga kasalukuyang opisyal. Gamitin ang panahong ito upang mas pagbutihin ang serbisyo, tapusin ang mga nasimulang programa at mas tutukan ang pangangailangan ng bawat komunidad, pamilya at kabataan," sabi ni Marcos sa Facebook page.
"Hindi ito dagdag na panahon sa puwesto. Dagdag itong panahon ng pananagutan sa taumbayan," dagdag pa niya.

Ipinasa ng Kongreso ang panukalang nagpapaliban sa nalalapit na BSKE at nagpapalawig sa termino ng mga opisyal sa limang taon. Ipinadala ang naturang batas sa Palasyo noong Huwebes para pirmahan ni Marcos upang ganap nang maging batas.
Kinumpirma rin ni Palace Press Officer Claire Castro ang paglagda sa panukala sa isang press briefing noong Biyernes.
“Pinirmahan na po ng Pangulo,” sabi ni Castro nang tanungin sa media briefing sa Ilocos Norte.
Sinabi ni Castro na kapuwa nakita ng Pangulo at mga mambabatas kung gaano kahalaga ang mga opisyal ng barangay, kabilang na sa paglaban sa kriminalidad at pagpapanatili ng kalinisan sa mga lansangan.

Ipinaliwanag din niya na nagbibigay-daan ang mas mahabang termino upang maisakatuparan ng mga opisyal ang mga pangmatagalang proyekto. Aniya, hindi ipinasa ang bagong batas para maging tamad ang mga opisyal.
“Ito ay para sila magtrabaho. Kaya para sa mga barangay officials, ang kailangan po namin ay trabaho mula sa inyo,” ani Castro.
Sa bagong batas, itinakda ang bagong petsa ng BSKE sa ikalawang linggo ng November 2028. Dapat sana itong gawin sa unang Lunes sa darating na Nobyembre.
Inaasahan naman na iaakyat ng mga kontra sa pagpapaliban ng naturang halalan ang usapin sa Korte Suprema. – FRJ GMA News

articles.title: Gilas Women fall short of Asian Games 3×3 gold vs hot-shooting Japan
articles.summary: Kacey dela Rosa puts Gilas Women on her back, but Japan proves too much to handle, pulling away for the convincing win behind its hot shooting to deal the Philippines its only loss in the Asian Games

blocks.text: SQUAD. Gilas Women in action in the women's 3x3 basketball competition in the 2026 Asian Games.
PSC-POC Media Pool
Kacey dela Rosa puts Gilas Women on her back, but Japan proves too much to handle, pulling away for the convincing win behind its hot shooting to deal the Philippines its only loss in the Asian Games

MANILA, Philippines – Gilas Women fell short of the Philippines’ third gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games after a stinging 21-11 loss to host Japan in the women’s 3×3 basketball final at the Kinjo Futo Station Square Venue in Nagoya on Friday, September 25.

Kacey dela Rosa put the the Filipinas on her back with 6 points, 3 rebounds, and 3 blocks, but the Japanese proved too much to handle, pulling away for the convincing win behind their hot shooting from beyond the arc.
Yuki Hirashita and Sakura Horiuchi fired 9 and 8 points, respectively, and each sank three two-pointers — the two taking turns in torching the Philippines.
Dela Rosa kept Gilas Women within striking distance with a bucket that cut their deficit to 8-12 before Japan closed out the win on a 9-3 run with 30 seconds to spare.
Hirashita scattered 5 points during that stretch, including the two-pointer that sealed the victory for Japan.
Amyah Espano put up 3 points and 3 rebounds in the silver finish, Kennan Ka added 2 points and 4 rebounds, while Maria Pasilang contributed 4 rebounds.
Despite the heartbreaking ending as they absorbed their only loss in the tournament, Gilas Women delivered the Philippines its first-ever 3×3 basketball medal in the Asian Games.
Meanwhile, Gilas Men missed out on the bronze after a 21-10 defeat to Iran.
Doy Dungo churned out 4 points, Luis Pablo tallied 3 points and 2 rebounds, Nic Cabañero had 2 points and 1 rebound, while Koji Buenaflor chimed in 1 point for the Philippines.
It was a disappointing result for Gilas Men after they won their first four games only to drop their last two matches, losing to South Korea in the semifinals and then to Iran. – Rappler.com

articles.title: How the illegal dumping of toxic waste in a Croatian town sparked national calls for clean-up
articles.summary:
After years of illegal mass flytipping in Gospić, fed-up residents decided to take matters into their own hands

“Gospić is our home,” Željka Šikić shouted to a crowd of 40,000 people outside…

blocks.text: “Gospić is our home,” Željka Šikić shouted to a crowd of 40,000 people outside the Croatian parliament earlier this month. The slogan is the name of a campaign she helped to set up to protest against the illegal dumping of waste in Gospić, a town in the mountainous Lika region of central Croatia.

Between 2022 and 2024, waste was illegally abandoned at several sites in the town. At one of the biggest, just 50 metres from Šikić’s home, an estimated 35,000 tonnes of waste, some of it hazardous, was dumped and buried.

In the dead of night, lorries heaving with waste would pass her front door and enter a nearby industrial site. This activity went largely unnoticed by the local authorities and police. But residents in Gospić were well aware and started taking it in turns to stay up to photograph the vehicles coming in and out of the site.
“I don’t think it should be our job to stay awake all night to see what’s going on,” Šikić says.

blocks.caption: An illegal waste site in Gospić in August. Photograph: Pixsell/Alamy

blocks.text: The waste became a blight on the community and a recent report from the Croatian Institute of Public Health revealed Pfas “forever chemicals” had been detected in groundwater samples nearby. Elevated concentrations of copper and lead were also detected in the soil.

Pfas are a group of thousands of synthetic chemicals that have been linked to serious health conditions, including several types of cancer. They are known as “forever chemicals” because of how long they persist in the environment.
Despite assurances that their drinking water is safe, a lack of trust means many residents have resorted to buying bottled water.
“I’m really scared,” Šikić says. “I would like to move house but I don’t know who would pay for the house on the first road next to the waste. I feel betrayed.”

blocks.caption: Residents took to filming lorries going in and out of one of the dumping sites on the outskirts of Gospić, seen here last month. Photograph: Pixsell/Alamy

blocks.text: In February 2025, years after the activity began, police and law enforcement officers arrested 13 people on suspicion of being part of the environmental criminal network involved in dumping the waste.

The main suspects, two Croatian nationals, were considered high-value targets by Europol and were believed to have orchestrated the illegal import of hazardous waste from Italy, Slovenia and Germany. It is thought the criminals generated upwards of €4m (£3.4m) in profit from this activity.

Waste crime is big business. Criminal networks often take advantage of the high costs associated with treating and disposing of waste properly. By falsifying documents to declare the waste as destined for recycling, they can save on the costs and pocket the difference.
Residents in Gospić had hoped the arrests would finally mean the site was shut down and cleaned up. But 18 months later, it is still there.
Frustrated by the lack of action, Šikić and 16 other residents joined together to form the “Gospić is our home” movement.

Ivana Rukavina Sarić, another member of the campaign group, says: “We called people from different professional backgrounds because we knew from the beginning that this would be highly complicated and would need a multi-disciplinary approach.”
after newsletter promotion
Having shared information about their struggles online and with Croatian media, Sarić says the campaign turned national, with the group now getting calls daily from other affected communities.

“There are so many waste hotspots in the whole of Croatia and so many people facing similar problems. The problem we have in Gospić is the drop of liquid that overflows the glass,” she says. “It’s become a national, even global problem.”

Similar dumping has been reported in several other Croatian towns, but the issue extends far beyond national borders. The United Nations estimates that 15% to 30% of EU waste shipments are illegal, and a recent investigation by the Guardian uncovered irrigation canals contaminated with microplastics in Turkey, a major destination for UK waste exports.

blocks.caption: What began as a small local campaign has grown into a national movement, with thousands attending a demonstration about the issue in Zagreb this month. Photograph: Ronald Gorsic/Cropix/SIPA/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Anger at the scale of the problem prompted tens of thousands of people from across Croatia to descend on the capital on 5 September. It is thought there were upwards of 40,000 people marching through Zagreb. “The capital was full,” Sarić says.

The group is demanding a comprehensive remediation of the site and the urgent removal of the buried waste. It also wants all known waste hotspots in Croatia to be included in a national waste strategy.

The government has opened two public procurement procedures for the removal, disposal or recovery of the waste. But with the waste still there four years since the illegal activity began, and concerns mounting over potential health and environmental impacts, the group plans to head to Brussels where it will protest at the European parliament.
“We’ve lost so much time, we don’t have time for more promises,” Sarić says. “We want clear information, clear deadlines and clear action.”
The Croatian government did not respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: Yukon's rural health centres without a nurse for 214 days during year-long period, CBC analysis finds
articles.summary: Data provided to CBC News from the territorial health department suggests the Yukon government is still struggling to staff rural health centres across the territory.

image.caption: The health centre in Ross River, Yukon. It's one of several rural health centres in the territory that have seen temporary closures or service disruptions over the last year. (Chloé Dioré de Périgny/CBC)

blocks.text: North
Data provided to CBC News from the territorial health department suggests the Yukon government is still struggling to staff rural health centres across the territory.
No nurse on site 214 days across the Yukon’s community health centres over past year
The Yukon’s rural health centres continue to struggle with temporary closures and disruptions.
This week, the territory's health department verified the number of interruptions to its community health centres over the past year.

According to CBC’s analysis of the data provided by the department, between August 2025 and August 2026 the territory's rural health centres saw a total of 214 days when there were no nursing services available.

That tally doesn’t totally reflect the latest partial closure at the Beaver Creek health centre from July 2 to Oct. 30. It also leaves out “reduced services” at the Carcross health centre from Sept. 16 to Oct. 14.
Furthermore, Faro is seeing a temporary closure from Sept. 25 to Oct. 2, Ross River from Sept. 4 to Sept 30, and Teslin from Sept. 23 to Oct. 14.

As the Official Opposition, the Yukon Party previously railed against the former Liberal government for its failure to keep health centres open for prolonged periods of time. During last year's election campaign, Currie Dixon, now the premier, vowed that his party was "going to change this.”
Lack of community nurses goes on
Beaver Creek's health centre saw the most days of closure or reduced service over the past year, at 82.
Pelly Crossing and Destruction Bay have also seen significant disruptions.
The problem is marked by a lack of nurses available to work at the rural health centres. It’s been a chronic issue for the community centres which aren't regularly staffed by physicians.
According to the health department, some services are still available during some health centre closures.

The department said in a statement that depending on the community, emergency services were still available, administrative staff could help with medical travel and bookings, and doctor clinics went on.
Health Minister Brad Cathers wasn’t available for an interview.
The health department said the model of community care is under review.

The government also said it’s continually looking for ways to recruit and keep nurses working in the territory, and expanding licensing pathways for qualified health professionals. It’s also “evaluating opportunities” for a more sustainable health-care system in communities.
National nurses association hears some frustration

Valerie Grdisa, CEO of the Canadian Nurses Association, travelled to the Yukon at the end of June and she spoke with dozens of nurses at Whitehorse General Hospital and also met with the health centre team in Carcross.
Grdisa said she heard about pride and innovation in the workplace, as well as frustrations around the ability to retain nurses who want to live and provide care in the communities.

Grdisa said nurses aren’t regularly considering the ability to get licensed and be registered in multiple jurisdictions. She added that there’s actually a rather large workforce in the country, with 518,000 registered or regulated nurses in Canada.
“I think we could do a better job in providing opportunities for people to be more mobile,” she said.
Grdisa also suggested health centres look to hire closer to home.

“I think the homegrown workforce pathways are the way to go, so investing in youth engagement,” she said. “We're talking in the middle schools and high schools, and then having local education programs and apprenticeships and return-of-service agreements.”
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Dana Hatherly is a reporter at CBC Yukon. She previously worked for the Yukon News from January 2022 to 2026.
With files from Chris MacIntyre and Dave White

articles.title: Marcos suspends excise taxes on LPG, kerosene anew
articles.summary: The tax relief does not extend to gasoline and diesel, as Finance Secretary Frederick Go says this would 'not be progressive' because higher-income consumers who use more of the two fuels would…

blocks.text: A worker unloads tanks of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) at a store in Paco, Manila, on January 30, 2023.
Rappler

The tax relief does not extend to gasoline and diesel, as Finance Secretary Frederick Go says this would 'not be progressive' because higher-income consumers who use more of the two fuels would capture more of the benefit

items: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has suspended excise taxes on liquid petroleum gas (LPG) and kerosene due to high global oil prices, effective immediately upon publication.
The suspension lasts a maximum of three months and does not apply to gasoline or diesel, which have seen significant price increases.
The measure will be reviewed monthly by the Development Budget Coordination Committee and the Department of Energy to determine its continuation or modification.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered the full suspension of excise taxes on liquid petroleum gas (LPG) and kerosene as high global oil prices continue to hit the wallets of Filipino consumers; the relief, however, does not extend to gasoline or diesel.

Marcos issued Executive Order No. 125 on Friday, September 25, following a recommendation from the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC). The order will take effect immediately upon publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation.

The suspension covers LPG, except when used as a raw material for petrochemical production or for motive power, and kerosene, except when used as aviation fuel. Gasoline and diesel, which have seen successive sharp price increases in recent weeks, were not included in the tax break.

blocks.caption: Fuel prices rise again with big hike on September 22

blocks.text: The relief can last a maximum of three months, but may end earlier if the one-month average price of Dubai crude falls below the $80-per-barrel level.

The move came after the Department of Energy (DOE) certified that one-month average Dubai crude price had reached $99.41 per barrel, well above the $80-per-barrel threshold required for the government to suspend fuel excise taxes. The DBCC subsequently recommended full suspension.
The DBCC and DOE are also required to review the measure every month and may recommend whether the suspension should continue, be modified, or ended.

Finance Secretary Frederick Go earlier told senators that suspending excise taxes on gasoline and diesel would “not be progressive,” given that wealthier consumers use more of the two fuels and would capture a larger share of the benefit. The government could also lose about P12 billion in tax revenues each month if the break was extended to gasoline and diesel.

The government previously suspended excise taxes on LPG and kerosene for three months beginning in April after Dubai crude similarly breached the trigger threshold. Gasoline and diesel were also excluded from that earlier round.

The Department of Finance previously estimated that suspending excise taxes for LPG and kerosene for the maximum three-month period would cost the government around P4.1 billion in foregone revenues. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Jay-Z rape accuser says her allegation was false
articles.summary: A woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 now says she has never met the rap superstar.

blocks.text: A woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 has formally said her allegation was untrue.
The unnamed woman filed a lawsuit in 2024 claiming she had been drugged and raped by Jay-Z, real name Shawn Carter, and Sean "Diddy" Combs at a party after the MTV Video Music Awards in 2000.
The stars denied the allegation and she dropped the lawsuit last year. Carter then sued her and her lawyers.

In a statement filed in that case on Thursday, she wrote: "Shawn 'Jay-Z' Carter never raped me. I have never met or spoken to Mr. Carter. Mr. Carter never engaged in any inappropriate conduct toward me whatsoever."

The woman, known in court documents by the pseudonym Jane Doe, also said: "My claims that Mr Carter and Mr Combs raped me while a third celebrity, [name redacted] watched are false. There is no truth to any of my claims against Mr Carter.
"I understand my false accusations have caused Mr Carter immense pain, suffering, and damage that can never be fully undone."
Carter had vehemently denied the accusations, saying they were a "blackmail attempt" and describing them as "frivolous, fictitious and appalling allegations".
When the accuser dropped her case in February 2025, the rapper, who is married to singer Beyoncé, said: "The trauma that my wife, my children, loved ones and I have endured can never be dismissed."
The woman, from Alabama, has now been removed from Carter's lawsuit.
She said she had not received any money from the rap superstar or anyone acting on his behalf, and had not been paid to make her latest declaration.
The rapper is still suing the woman's former lawyers, led by Tony Buzbee.
In a statement to Rolling Stone, external, which first reported Jane Doe's new declaration, Buzbee said he had not seen it.

He said: "We have multiple lawyers (at least four) who dealt with Ms Doe long before she met me. She gave the exact same story to each. If for some reason now she is claiming she lied to us and the court, that's new information."

When Carter filed his lawsuit against the woman and her lawyers in February 2025, Buzbee claimed at the time that Carter's investigators had "repeatedly harassed, threatened and harangued this poor woman for weeks, trying to intimidate her and make her recant her story".
In her new declaration, the woman said: "I never received any threat from Mr Carter or anyone acting on his behalf."

Setting out the events that led to her allegation, the woman said she saw an advert on Facebook in September or October 2024 looking for people who might have sexual assault claims against Combs. "The ad triggered memories of being raped when I was 13 years old," she said.
She was contacted by a law firm but was not provided with a draft of the lawsuit containing her allegations and did not authorise it before it was filed in October 2024, she said.

She also said Buzbee and other lawyers acting on her behalf filed it "without conducting any independent investigation, background inquiry, or due diligence, and without obtaining any corroboration of the allegations".
She said: "The October Complaint alleges that Mr Carter and Mr Combs raped me when I was a minor while an unnamed celebrity watched. As discussed above, these allegations were false."
Buzbee also represents numerous other people who have made allegations against Combs.
Combs denied Jane Doe's claims, which his lawyer described at the time as one of a number of civil cases "pushed forward by an attorney more focused on media headlines than legal merit".
In July 2025, Combs was convicted by a criminal court on prostitution-related charges involving his two ex-girlfriends, and is currently serving a four-year prison sentence.
The BBC has contacted Buzbee for comment.

articles.title: Mary Jane Veloso’s counsel expects faster release after Marcos’ ‘unique’ absolute pardon
articles.summary: Veloso's lawyer explained that unlike their other clients who were released due to dismissal of cases or acquittal, Veloso’s case is the first time that the President itself had ordered the…

blocks.text: September 25, 2026 | 6:43pm

MANILA, Philippines — Mary Jane Veloso’s legal counsel is expecting the process for her release to be faster than usual, stressing that the pardon granted by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is an “absolute prerogative” that is beyond review.

Veloso’s counsel and National Union of People’s Lawyer (NUPL) Chairperson Edre Olalia said on Friday, September 25, that they are yet to navigate the specific protocols for her release because of the "unique" circumstances of her case.

“I hope and we expect that it’s going to be anytime. But of course, the devil’s in the details. Because this is a unique case, it has no precedent as far as we know,” Olalia said in an interview with ANC.
The lawyer explained that unlike their other clients who were released due to dismissal of cases or acquittal, Veloso’s case is the first time that the president itself had ordered the release.
In this case, he added, the nature of the pardon granted cannot be challenged and no longer needs review from other government branches and agencies, since the order came from Marcos himself.
“The term itself means what it is; it’s absolute. So there is no legal impediment,” Olalia added. “For us, we envisioned it’s going to be faster than what we have handled before.”
Reuniting with Mary Jane
Marcos revealed earlier Friday that he had signed the absolute pardon for Veloso, effectively ensuring the end of her 16-year imprisonment.
Veloso’s family celebrated Marcos’ announcement and thanked the president, describing it as a realization of their hope and answer to their long-standing prayers.

“Talagang masayang-masaya po. Iyan po talaga ang hinihintay namin, ‘yung mapirmahan na ng ating pangulo ang paglaya ng aking anak,” Cesar Veloso, Mary Jane’s father, said in a separate interview with ANC.
(We are truly happy. That is what we are waiting for, for the president to grant my daughter’s freedom.)
According to Cesar, their family, along with Mary Jane’s two children, is hoping to personally welcome her in her release.
“Pasasayahin daw po nila ang kanilang Mama pagka-dumating. Kaya ‘yung hindi po nila nagawa noon, gagawin po nila ngayon,” Cesar said.
(They said they will make their mother happy when she arrives. The things they were unable to do before, they will do now.)
Fruit of the struggle
Lawmakers also celebrated the granting of the pardon and Veloso’s anticipated release.
Sen. Francisco “Kiko” Pangilinan said in a statement that the pardon gave Veloso and her family a chance to start a new life.

“Matapos ang mahabang pagkakahiwalay, unti-unti nang mabibigyan ng pagkakataon si Mary Jane at ang kanyang pamilya na mabawi ang panahong nawala sa kanila — at muling simulan ang buhay na matagal nilang ipinagdasal,” Pangilinan said.
Solons from the House of Representatives, meanwhile, said the pardon is a hard-won victory and a fruit of the long struggle of migrant workers and human rights defenders.
“This is very welcome news, especially for Mary Jane Veloso and her family. Long-overdue freedom and justice,” Mamamayang Liberal (ML) Party-list Rep. Leila De Lima said in a statement.

Veloso was sentenced to death by firing squad in Indonesia in 2010 as authorities found 2.6 kilograms of heroin in her suitcase. She was then given a last-minute reprieve and was repatriated to the Philippines in 2014.
Meanwhile, Gabriela Party-list Rep. Sarah Elago stressed that Veloso’s victory does not end the fight of migrant workers against illegal recruiters and human traffickers.

“Ito po ay isang laban na hindi pa nagtatapos. Kasi sa tingin natin dapat wala nang muli na tulad ni Mary Jane Veloso na biktima ng human trafficking, na biktima ng pagsasamantala, ang magsa-suffer sa matagal na panahon ng inhustisya,” Elago said.

articles.title: Hurricane Polo barrels towards Baja California region of Mexico
articles.summary:
Area’s second-most intense hurricane on record being fuelled by exceptionally warm Pacific waters

Hurricane Polo is barreling towards the Baja California region of Mexico, the latest system…

blocks.text: Hurricane Polo is barreling towards the Baja California region of Mexico, the latest system in a Pacific hurricane season that has been notably active in recent months. On 22 September, a measurement of 892 millibars was registered for Hurricane Polo, making it the second-most intense hurricane on record in the east Pacific. It is fuelled by exceptionally warm waters across the Pacific Ocean, providing favourable conditions for the system to maintain its considerable strength.

Polo is expected to turn towards the west-north-west, before taking a more north-westerly trajectory on Saturday. It has maximum sustained winds of around 150mph, with even stronger gusts occurring within the most intense parts of the hurricane. Hurricane-force winds extend outward for approximately 40 miles from the centre, while tropical storm-force winds reach as far as 125 miles. These powerful winds, combined with torrential rainfall and dangerous seas, could have significant impacts. Although some fluctuations in intensity are possible over the coming days, Polo is expected to remain powerful as it tracks north-westwards.

In India, a deep 988-millibar low-pressure system – a tropical storm in this case – is centred along the east coast, bringing widespread and potentially disruptive weather conditions to Odisha and surrounding areas. The system is producing heavy rainfall across the region, with the latest forecast models suggesting totals could exceed 200mm in some locations over a 24-hour period. Rainfall rates are expected to be particularly intense at times, with hourly totals potentially exceeding 30mm in the heaviest downpours. Such intense rainfall could cause significant surface water and localised flooding, particularly in low-lying areas and places with poor drainage. Strong and gusty winds are also affecting coastal parts of Odisha. Winds are forecast to reach around 50-60mph, creating hazardous conditions in exposed areas and potentially causing disruption to travel, infrastructure and power supplies. Authorities have closed numerous schools across the affected districts for safety reasons.

Meanwhile, in Iberia, the relentless heat of summer is extending into meteorological autumn, with temperatures rising into the high 30s celsius on 23 September. Alvega, in Portugal, recorded a maximum temperature of 41.7C, smashing many July records from previous decades.

articles.title: Is Vince Dizon still in — or out — as DPWH chief?
articles.summary: 'Ovedue na po kayo ng ilang araw,' Senator Imee Marcos tells DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon

blocks.text: DPWH CHIEF. Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon leads the agency's flag-raising ceremony on October 20, 2025.
James Patrick Cruz/Rappler
'Ovedue na po kayo ng ilang araw,' Senator Imee Marcos tells DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon
It’s been more than a year since President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. tapped Vince Dizon to lead and clean up the corruption-tainted Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).
But during the agency’s budget hearing at the Senate on Friday, September 25, Senator Imee Marcos raised a rather basic question: Is Dizon still legally in charge of DPWH?

Citing the Administrative Code of 1987, Marcos pointed out that a temporary designation in an acting capacity should not exceed one year. The safeguard is meant to prevent acting appointments from being used to circumvent the Commission on Appointments.
Dizon was appointed acting DPWH secretary on September 1, 2025, after his brief stint as transportation secretary.
On September 2, Marcos also sent a letter asking about the status of Dizon’s appointment. Dizon, apologetic, said he had yet to see the letter.
“Baka may appointment na kayo,” Marcos asked. (Maybe you already have an appointment.)
Dizon said his appointment as secretary continues until Congress adjourns and goes into recess. After that, he said, he would need to be reappointed.
Marcos, however, pointed back to the Administrative Code.
“Overdue na po kayo ng ilang araw,” (You’re already overdue for a few days) she told Dizon. “What’s the present status of your appointment?”
Dizon’s answer? He wasn’t exactly the person who could give it.
“Madam Senator, unfortunately, I’m not the appointing authority. I will confirm with the Office of the President and ask,” he said.
And who is the appointing authority? Marcos Jr., the senator’s estranged younger brother.
Senator Marcos then pressed Dizon on the legal basis for continuing to head the DPWH.
“If your appointment has lapsed, what’s the legal basis of appearing here?” she asked Dizon, whom she referred to as a friend.
Dizon’s explanation for why he was sitting there at the DPWH budget hearing?
“I’m here because I guess I’m not yet fired,” he said, while holding the back of his neck.
Marcos then asked if Dizon had been reappointed without anyone knowing. Marcos then cited information they had received that Dizon had been “appointed or reappointed” on July 27.
Dizon said he was not aware of any reappointment. According to his chief of staff, however, he could still perform his duties at the DPWH.
And despite the awkward questions over whether he still had the authority to lead the agency, Dizon appeared remarkably unfazed.
In fact, he seemed almost relieved by the possibility that his stint at the DPWH was over.

“Ma’am, this is music to my ears kasi medyo ayoko na rin pong nandito ako. Gusto ko pong wala na ako dito. Okay na po ito. Masaya pa po ako,” Dizon said. (Ma’am, this is music to my ears because, to be honest, I’m also getting tired of being here. I want to no longer be here. This is fine with me. I’d even be happy.)

“To be quite frank, it will be welcome kung totoo po ’yung sinasabi ninyo na hindi na ako secretary ng DPWH. I’ll be more than happy to accept that kasi napakahirap po ng trabahong ito,” he said. (To be quite frank, it would be welcome if what you’re saying is true that I’m no longer the DPWH secretary. I’d be more than happy to accept that because this job is extremely difficult.)
So is he in or out? – Rappler.com

articles.title: Villanueva wants firing squad for guilty in flood control scheme
articles.summary: Senator Joel Villanueva on Friday called for those proven guilty in the alleged flood control scam to face the firing squad. “I am always for justice. Until now, gusto ko ngang i-firing squad yung…

blocks.text: Published September 25, 2026 6:10pm
Senator Joel Villanueva on Friday called for those proven guilty in the alleged flood control scam to face the firing squad.

During the Senate budget hearing for the Commission on Higher Education and state universities and colleges, Villanueva asked University of the Philippines Resilience Institute executive director Mahar Lagmay whether there were better ways to forecast extreme weather events.
Villanueva then expressed frustration over recurring flooding in his home province of Bulacan before turning to the alleged flood control scam, in which he had previously been linked.

“God knows, and until now, some people thought that I have a case on this. Until now wala ‘ho akong case. May complaints, etc. tinuturo na kasama ako ngayon… and I’m not scared to talk about this,” Villanueva said.
(God knows, and until now, some people thought that I have a case on this. Until now, I do not have a case. There are complaints, etc. and I am being implicated… I am not afraid to talk about this.)

“I am always for justice. Until now, gusto ko ngang i-firing squad iyong lahat ng may kaso dito na talagang mapapatunayan na parte nitong scheme na ito, itong kalokohan na ito, itong kabulastugan na nangyari dahil number one na naapektuhan yung probinsya namin sa Bulacan,” Villanueva said.

(I am always for justice, I want a firing squad for all those who have a case in this and will be proven guilty that they have a part in this scheme, this bluff because number one affected is our province of Bulacan.)
Villanueva said that the records would show that he spent years asking the Department of Public Works and Highways for an integrated flood control program.

During the height of the flood control issue in 2025, dismissed Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) district engineer Henry Alcantara tagged several lawmakers in the multi-billion corruption scheme. — including Villanueva.
Alcantara claimed that he brought P150 million to a rest house in Bulacan, which was allegedly received by one of Villanueva’s staff.
No formal charges have been lodged against the Bulacan senator.

Accused alongside him were Sen. Jinggoy Estrada and former senator Bong Revilla. Both of whom were indicted for charges in relation to the flood control scam. While Revilla was able to post bail, Estrada remains incarcerated at the Quezon City Jail.
The Philippines abolished the death penalty in 2006 under Republic Act No. 9346, replacing capital punishment with life imprisonment and reclusion perpetua.—LDF, GMA News
